fun_highlights: The four vocations (soldier/scholar/maker/wanderer) are the single biggest structural win: a soldier's life genuinely reads differently from a scholar's, with dedicated adult/midlife/elder card clusters that accumulate into a coherent arc rather than a loose pile of moments.

Era-gated cards (war/plague/plenty/hard/turning) inject macro-level variety at no cost to the player — a plague life and a settled life open differently from the first year, and the era can change at succession so gen-3 and gen-8 of the same dynasty can feel historically distinct.

Callback cards (cb_books_late, cb_outcast_return, cb_lookaway, cb_study_pays, cb_strayed, etc.) are the most structurally novel idea in the game: they reach twenty or thirty years back to a specific earlier choice and close a personal arc. When they fire they feel like a genuine narrative payoff that could not have happened in a different run — 'A kindness done at 6 came back, decades later, as a door held open' after the c_friend choice is the game at its best.

Trait affinity on card draws means a bookish child genuinely leans toward c_book, a warm one toward c_friend, a restless one toward c_steal/c_move — childhood is not a uniform checklist but a fingerprint of who this particular child already is.

The dynasty layer (seat, repute, motto, heirlooms, secret, era) genuinely accumulates: House Vane with motto 'We give past what we can spare' and the inherited book heirloom landing in Edmund and then Tariq's midlife is a cross-life payoff that no single-life game can do.

Once-per-dynasty (onceDyn) gating is smart design: c_sick, y_mentor, m_parent_age, e_legacy, cb_left_home and others fire at most once across a whole house, so a 5-generation dynasty does not replay identical milestone beats in every life.

Early death variety and voluntary childlessness (Adaline at 23, Henrik at 19, Cassian at 44, Tamsin refusing marriage, Tobias choosing no children initially) mean life-shape is not always the full arc — truncated lives and divergent family structures read as real variety, not padding.
staleness: The love-marriage-child sequence is structurally almost universal. Scanning all 15 dynasties (~30 individual lives): the overwhelming majority follow the pattern of [meet love in youth or as late-adult] → [a_marry] → [a_child]. The age varies but the SEQUENCE does not. A life without love at all is rare in the transcripts; childlessness is rarer still. The engine nudges these cards strongly enough that a variety-seeker notices the domestic skeleton under every life by dynasty 5.

The scholar legacy card (m_scholar_legacy: 'give it all away vs guard it') appears in Selma, Emory, Soren (Marchetti), Vera (Okonkwo), Junia, Lazlo (Reyes), and Annika — seven out of fifteen dynasties — with functionally identical prose every time. The same applies to cb_books_late (the 'old book on a high shelf' callback): it fires in Annika (D8), Edmund (D8), Tariq Vane (D8), Idris (D13), Lazlo (D14), Soren (D13) — the reader's eye learns to skip it. When a callback fires in nearly every scholar-adjacent life it stops being a callback and becomes furniture.

The 'someone Ambrose/Cosima/X helped once, years ago, is somebody now' outcast-return callback (cb_outcast_return) fires in Annika (D8 at 27), Cosima (D13 at 35), Theda (D13 at 28), Lazlo (D10 at 34), and the neighbour-kindness variant in Lazlo (D10 at 52). The prose template — 'A kindness done at AGE came back, decades later, as a door held open' — is nearly verbatim across all instances. After seeing it twice it is recognisable as a slot, not a surprise.

The elder arc is the least varied section of any life. After midlife the draw pool narrows sharply: e_reconcile, e_legacy, e_garden, e_window, e_last_walk, e_peace, e_body, e_bequest, e_craft, e_journey, e_old_letters, e_soldier_old, m_scholar_legacy, the scholar-peace card. Most lives see 3-4 of these from the same pool, producing elder sections that feel interchangeable across vocations. A soldier's elder life and a maker's elder life share almost the same final beats.

Fate-event cards (fire, grace/windfall, the 'college collapse' economic crash) have no choice — they are single-option narration beats. In the transcripts the fire card ('Lost the house... and learned the cold lesson of how fast a life's accumulation burns') appears in Tomas (D1), Vesna (D7), Vera (D11), and Lazlo (D14). With no player agency, seeing the same forced narration four times in a play-through is especially flat.

The 'no-marked-traits' lives (Ottilie D13, Henrik D12, Lazlo D14 gen-2) lack the trait-affinity draw weighting that differentiates bookish or warm or restless childhoods. Their childhood sections read as nearly identical: c_origin (take the world as it comes) → random card → random card → y_calling. Without a trait fingerprint these lives feel like blanks.

The 'cb_principle' callback (stand again for the old principle) fires in Ambrose (D1), Tomas (D1), Marguerite (D9), Tamsin (D11/D3), Theda (D13), Edmund (D8) — six lives — always with nearly the same framing ('The thing X stood up for once, young and at a cost, comes round again'). The payoff text is rotated but the structural beat is the same: youth principle → midlife echo. A variety-seeker stops experiencing it as a callback after the second or third instance.

The dynasty-memory card (d_ancestor) has only one functional shape: 'live up to the name vs step out of its shadow.' It rotates which ancestor is named but the binary choice and consequences are identical every time. By dynasty 8+ every player who took 'step out of its shadow' once and 'live up to the name' once has exhausted the novelty of this card entirely.

improvements.what: Break the love-marriage-child spine into genuinely optional tracks with different content in each. A confirmed-solitary life should get 3-4 cards exploring what that shape feels like (chosen celibacy, a platonic partnership, investing in work or community instead of family) rather than simply missing the domestic cards. Currently childlessness is modelled as an absence, not a presence.
improvements.why: The love/marry/child sequence is the single most visible repeated arc across all 15 dynasties. Giving the non-domestic path its own content means a variety-seeker faces genuinely different structural decisions rather than the same fork with one road blocked.

improvements.what: The fate-only cards (fire, economic crash, grace-from-a-stranger) need a player choice or they should be retired. At minimum give the fire card a second option ('salvage one thing before it burns' vs 'let it all go') and the crash card a decision about what to cut. Single-outcome narration cards feel like cutscenes and are the most visibly repeated beats in the transcripts.
improvements.why: Four fire appearances and three grace-from-stranger appearances in 15 dynasties, all with no agency, is the most direct staleness signal. A choice does not need to be dramatic — even a small decision about how to respond rescues the card from feeling like a plot railroad.

improvements.what: Cap the cb_books_late / scholar-legacy / outcast-return callbacks at once per DYNASTY (onceDyn), not once per life. These callbacks currently fire freely in every scholar-adjacent life, which removes the surprise of recognition that is the callback's whole point.
improvements.why: The book-on-the-shelf callback fires in six separate lives across eight dynasties in the transcripts. When a 'personal' memory payoff becomes predictable infrastructure it degrades from callback to routine.

improvements.what: Add 3-4 elder cards that are vocation-exclusive and structurally different from the universal pool: a wanderer's elder cards about what rootlessness costs at 75, a soldier's PTSD-settled cards about making peace with what was done, a scholar's specific regret/pride beats. Currently all elder arcs converge on the same 6-7 cards regardless of the life lived.
improvements.why: The elder section is where variety-seekers notice most strongly that they are watching the same template. Vocation-specific elder content is already partially implemented (e_soldier_old, e_maker_handoff) but needs depth — these single cards cannot carry a 15-20 year span against the universal pool.

improvements.what: Give the d_ancestor dynasty-memory card 3-4 distinct framings beyond 'live up to / step out of.' For example: a life that chose the hard path might receive the ancestor's story as a warning; a scholar house might have the ancestor's unanswered question resurface as a puzzle; a tainted house might have the ancestor appear in a way that makes the player implicate themselves in the old wrong.
improvements.why: The current binary is exhausted after two encounters. Making the dynasty-memory card respond to what THIS life has already done (via cond checking current flags/memories) would make it feel like genuine generational echo rather than a reusable shell.

improvements.what: Add 2-3 late-adult (age 50-65) cards that only appear for lives WITHOUT a spouse or children — not absence-of-domestic-arc but presence of a different kind of midlife. A chosen-solitary at 55 faces different stakes than a married parent at 55, and the card pool should reflect that.
improvements.why: Currently the adult band fills for domestic lives with a_work, a_child (×2-3), a_marry, m_parent_age, m_child_grown, m_estrange. Non-domestic lives miss most of these and end up with visibly thinner adult sections. The a_fallow and m_empty_house cards gesture at this but do not fill the gap.

verdict: A Life has real structural ambition — vocations, eras, callbacks, dynasty reputation — that produces genuine variety across the first four or five dynasties, but the love-marriage-child spine is nearly universal, a handful of callbacks (book-on-shelf, outcast-return, stand-again) fire so frequently they lose the quality of surprise, and the elder arc converges to the same half-dozen cards regardless of the life lived, leaving a variety-seeker tracking recognisable slots rather than discovering new shapes by dynasty 8.
